title: reduce GPU memory usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
author: Aditi Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce peak GPU memory and workspace fragmentation during long-running streaming/inference workloads by combining targeted activation checkpointing, smaller per-op scratch buffers, and arena allocator heuristics. This PR introduces: 1) selective activation checkpointing on transformer blocks with minimal recompute overhead; 2) dynamic per-kernel scratch buffer sizing and reuse across attention/FFN kernels; 3) arena allocator tuning to reduce fragmentation for variable-length KV cache; 4) minor kernel refactors to expose max-scratch requirements to the allocator; 5) a memory-usage regression test that simulates continuous batching and KV cache growth. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-2783) - [x] unit + perf tests added - [x] backwards-compatible defaults (feature gated) - [x] release notes drafted Related work: builds on earlier arena changes in pr-33210 and activation checkpointing experiments in pr-31457. Expected impact: ~12-25% reduction in peak GPU memory for 8k context models in our internal perf lab when continuous batching + KV growth are present, and up to 10% reduction in tail latency due to lower OOM/backpressure events. Rollout plan: default disabled for dedicated/hosted until we validate at scale; opt-in via runtime config "enable_mem_tuning".

release_notes: Performance: reduced peak GPU memory for large context inference by enabling targeted activation checkpointing and arena tuning (opt-in).
Operational: new runtime flag enable_mem_tuning (default: false) to gate changes during rollout.
Testing: added continuous batching memory regression test to catch KV cache growth OOM regressions.
ci_summary: Perf CI: initial run flagged a test inversion (flaky) — rerun passed
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: activation checkpointing adds recompute cost and could increase latency for low-batch, low-latency use cases
Mitigation: feature is off by default and checkpointing is selective (only high-memory blocks), and we include a model-level opt-out flag
how_to_rollout: Step 1: deploy to perf lab and run memory_continuous_batching regression for a minimum of 48h
Step 2: canary on Dedicated pool with enable_mem_tuning=true for 1% traffic for 72h
Step 3: monitor token-level OOMs and tail latency; increase gradually to 10% if stable
notes: This PR intentionally keeps defaults conservative; primary benefit is for workloads with long contexts + continuous batching + KV cache growth.
Follow-ups: measure end-to-end cost impact and add an automated canary recipe in perf-canary repo.
